subject: Dedicated capacity: throughput guardrails, pricing, and rightsizing recommendation
messages:
From: Sofia Grant <sofia@ellumhealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated GPU sizing & pricing request

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for taking this — we ran the Q3 workload export and attached a short workbook with our traffic breakdown. High level: production chat + generative workflows, ~4M tokens/day, average conversation length ~1,800 tokens, and observed peak concurrency of ~280 (10-min window). We need a pricing path for a reserved capacity commit (12/24/36 month options), with an SLA for p99 latency and a burst buffer for infrequent spikes.

Questions we have:
- What GPU pool size do you recommend to meet p95 < 150ms for chat (1.8k tokens) and p99 < 300ms for generative flows?
- What are the discount thresholds by commit size / term?
- Can you accommodate a burst bucket for ~30% above committed throughput?

I've CC'd procurement. Attaching the workload export and one internal perf snapshot.

Thanks,
Sofia Grant
Director of Product — Ellum Health
sofia@ellumhealth.com

Attachments: Ellum_Workload_Report_Q3.xlsx, perf_snapshot.log

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Grant <sofia@ellumhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-11T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU sizing & pricing request

Hi Sofia — thanks for the workbook, looks comprehensive. I want to confirm a couple of quick items before Ben and Marissa run through a sizing calc:

1) Is the 4M tokens/day number inclusive of embeddings / async batch jobs or strictly real-time user chat + generation?
2) When you say "peak concurrency of ~280 (10-min window)", is that concurrent in-flight requests or concurrent active users (requests/sec observed)?
3) Any hard requirements for model family (e.g., families with 2k+ context, preference for quantized variants)?

Ben — can you run a baseline throughput estimate and a few packaging options (12/24/36 month commits + burst bucket) assuming 1.8k token average for chat and mixed 512–1k for generative flows? Marissa — can you prepare two pricing structures we can propose (commercial + technical bullets) and highlight recommended SLA guardrails.

I'll open a short meeting if we need to sync.

Best,
Hannah
Head of Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-12T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU sizing & pricing request

Quick calc notes (attached CSV): baseline assumptions
- Traffic: 4M tokens/day = ~46 tokens/sec average sustained (24/7). Peak observed window: 10-min with 280 concurrent in-flight requests
- Model: production LLM family (2k context), average generation per request ~350 tokens generated, chat includes 1.8k context reads for many requests
- HW: using Redwood A100-80 equiv baseline. Continuous batching gains assumed (20–40% depending on prefix reuse).

Sizing options (ballpark):
A) Conservative (low latency, headroom for growth)
- 8 x A100-80 (GPU pool)
- Supports ~300 concurrent low-latency chat-style requests with p95 ~130–160ms (depends on quant and batching).
- Recommended commit: 24 months or 36 months to unlock better discount tiers.

B) Cost-optimized (quantized + higher batch acceptance)
- 5 x A100-80 equivalent (or 10 x mid-tier GPUs with mixed packing)
- Expected p95 180–250ms, p99 may stretch during heavy spikes.

C) Pilot / short-term
- 3 x A100-80 equivalent with 30% burst bucket (credits) for spikes. We'd run a 6–8 week migration with live telemetry and then rightsize.

Burst handling: recommend a burst bucket equal to ~30% of committed throughput (consumable credits) for monthly peaks; automatic fallback to compatible, lower-cost model variants if pool saturated.

I'll attach the sizing CSV and a short latency/throughput model. Once Sofia confirms whether the peak 280 is in-flight RPS or active users I'll refine concurrency headroom and token-per-request mix.

—Ben
Sales Engineer — Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Attachments: Sizing_Calc_ellum_v1.csv

From: Sofia Grant <sofia@ellumhealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@ellumhealth.com
Date: 2026-10-13T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU sizing & pricing request

Thanks — thanks Ben. Clarifications:
- The 280 number is concurrent in-flight requests observed during a 10-minute spike window (not unique users).
- 4M tokens/day includes embeddings jobs (approx 300k tokens/day) but the majority is real-time chat/generative traffic (~3.7M).
- Model family: currently running a 2k+ context family, open to quantized variants but want parity for quality.

Procurement note: interested in a 24–36 month commit, but we'll need a pricing band and an approval-ready one-page summary that we can present to finance (highlighting effective discount, burst handling, and termination/scale clauses).

Sofia
Director of Product — Ellum Health

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-15T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU sizing & pricing request — recommended package

Summarizing for proposal (deliverable for Sofia/Procurement):

Technical recommendation (rightsized):
- Recommended commit footprint: 8 x A100-80 equivalent GPUs (can be delivered as larger counts of quantized A30/A10s depending on customer preference).
- Expected steady-state support: ~250–320 concurrent in-flight requests at mixed 1.8k chat / 512–1k gen profile with p95 latency target ~150ms (chat) and p99 ~280–320ms under sustained load. This assumes prefix caching and continuous batching configured for your workload.
- Burst policy: 30% monthly burst credits above committed throughput; credits draw from a monthly pool and to be used for infrequent peaks. Excess sustained usage billed at on-demand rate.

Commercial recommendation (three packaging paths):
1) 24-month Standard Commit — 8 GPU pool
   - Upfront commit: monthly billing at 28% discount vs list on-demand per-token unit economics
   - One-way scale-up option at pre-agreed pricing tiers; termination with 90-day notice + fair-market reconciliation.
2) 36-month Enterprise Commit — 8 GPU pool
   - Monthly billing at 35% discount (preferred) + 10% additional platform credit for onboarding/observability features
   - SLA: 99.9% uptime for Dedicated pool, p99 latency guardrails, quarterly performance review; included incident credits for violations.
3) Pilot (6–8 weeks) + Conversion — 3 GPU pilot with automatic conversion credits applied to first 6 months of a 24/36-month commitment if converted within 90 days.

Additional notes:
- We recommend a canary roll for cutover and a migration runbook (we can provide).
- We will propose a joint SLA addendum that defines measured p99 and the compensatory credit calculation.

I can turn this into a one-page pricing summary and a short commercial term sheet (redline-ready) for procurement. Thoughts on which packaging Sofia prefers?

—Marissa
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Grant <sofia@ellumhealth.com>, procurement@ellumhealth.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-19T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU sizing & pricing request — proposed next steps

Hi Sofia / Procurement team — thanks for the quick clarifications and patience. Attached is a one-page summary (commercial + technical) and the sizing CSV Ben prepared. High level recommendation:

- Target: 8 x A100-80 equivalent GPU pool delivered on a 24-month commit as the baseline. This balances latency headroom and cost predictability.
- Commercial: 24-month option at ~28% effective discount (as a band) vs on-demand; 36-month would move to ~35% and includes additional onboarding credits.
- Burst & SLA: 30% monthly burst credits + defined SLA guardrails; sustained overages billed at on-demand. We'll include a canary and migration runbook in the SOW.

Next steps I propose:
1) I'll share a one-page term summary and draft SOW for your legal/procurement to review (attach: Redwood_Dedicated_T&Cs_v2.pdf).
2) Schedule a 45-min technical alignment call (Ben + Marissa) to walk through canary, telemetry hooks, and performance expectations.
3) If procurement is comfortable with the commercial band, we can draft a subscription order form and route for signature — once signed we schedule onboarding and pilot cutover.

If you prefer, we can also provide an optional monitoring add-on (90 day extended logs for deeper regression tracing) for an additional credit.

Would Tuesday or Thursday next week work for the technical call?

Thanks — looking forward to getting you into Dedicated.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.com

Attachments: Redwood_Dedicated_T&Cs_v2.pdf, Sizing_Calc_ellum_v1.csv
